recipes.title: Luqaimat
recipes.summary: Crisp-shelled, fluffy fried dough balls scented with cardamom and saffron, drizzled with date syrup and sesame.

steps.text: Whisk the batter ingredients into a thick, smooth, sticky batter.
Cover and leave in a warm place until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil to 170 °C. Squeeze small balls of batter through your fist and scoop them off with a wet teaspoon into the oil (or use two spoons).
Fry, turning, until deep golden all over (4–5 minutes). Drain on paper.
Drizzle with date syrup and sprinkle with sesame. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Kabuli Palaw
recipes.summary: Afghanistan's national dish — lamb buried in spiced basmati rice, crowned with sweet caramelised carrots, raisins and nuts.
equipment: Heavy ovenproof pot with a lid

items.prep: on the bone, in large pieces
items.name: lamb shoulder

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then soak it.
Fry the onions in the oil until deep brown — this colours the dish. Add the lamb and brown it all over.
Add the water and salt and simmer, covered, until the lamb is tender.
Lift out the lamb. Measure 750 ml of the broth (top up with water if needed) and stir in the spices.
Meanwhile fry the carrots in 3 tablespoons of oil from the pot until soft, add the sugar and raisins and cook until the raisins plump. Toast the nuts in the same pan. Heat the oven to 160 °C.
Parboil the drained rice in salted boiling water for 4 minutes and drain. Put it in the pot with the spiced broth, nestle in the lamb, and cook uncovered over medium heat until the broth is absorbed.
Cover tightly and bake (the "dam" stage) until the rice is fluffy and separate.
Pile the rice on a platter with the lamb, and top with the carrots, raisins and nuts.

recipes.serving: On a large shared platter with salad and yogurt.

recipes.title: Tavë Kosi
recipes.summary: Albania's national dish — tender lamb baked under a thick, tangy yogurt and egg custard until golden.

steps.text: Season the lamb with salt and oregano. Brown it in the butter in an ovenproof dish, add the water, cover and roast at 180 °C until tender (about 60 minutes). Stir in the rice for the last 20 minutes, if using.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute. Cool slightly.
Whisk the yogurt and eggs together, then whisk in the butter-flour mixture, nutmeg and salt.
Pour the yogurt over the lamb.
Bake uncovered at 200 °C until set and golden on top.

recipes.title: Spas
recipes.summary: A soothing soup of tangy yogurt and hulled wheat, stabilised with egg and finished with butter-fried onion and dried mint.

steps.text: Simmer the barley in the water until tender.
Whisk the yogurt, egg, flour and salt until smooth in a pot.
Heat the yogurt mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction, until it comes to a simmer — the egg and flour stop it curdling.
Add the barley with its water and simmer 5 minutes.
Fry the onion in the butter until golden, add the mint off the heat, and pour over the soup. Add the herbs.

recipes.serving: Hot in winter or chilled in summer.

recipes.title: Muamba de Galinha
recipes.summary: Chicken stewed in red palm oil with okra, squash, tomato and garlic — Angola's national dish, eaten with funge.

steps.text: Season the chicken with lemon juice, garlic and salt and marinate.
Heat the palm oil over medium heat (don't let it smoke). Brown the chicken, then add the onions and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes, chili and water, cover and simmer.
Add the squash and okra and simmer until the chicken and vegetables are tender and the sauce has thickened.

recipes.serving: With funge (a stiff cassava- or corn-flour porridge) and beans.

recipes.title: Chimichurri
recipes.summary: A sharp, herby sauce of parsley, oregano, garlic, chili, vinegar and oil — the essential partner to Argentine grilled meat.

items.note: or a mix of olive and sunflower oil
items.name: olive oil

steps.text: Dissolve the salt in the hot water to make a brine (salmuera).
Combine the parsley, oregano, garlic and chili in a jar. Add the brine and vinegar, then the oil.
Leave at room temperature to let the flavours mingle.

tips: It improves over a day in the fridge and keeps for about a week.
recipes.serving: Spooned over asado (grilled beef), choripán (sausage sandwich) or grilled vegetables.

recipes.title: Wiener Schnitzel
recipes.summary: Thin veal cutlets in a puffy, golden breadcrumb coat, fried in plenty of fat and served with lemon.

items.note: about 140 g each, from the leg
items.name: veal cutlet

items.prep: beaten with 1 tbsp milk or cream
items.name: egg

items.note: or clarified butter or vegetable oil
items.name: lard

steps.text: Place each cutlet between sheets of plastic wrap and pound evenly to about 4 mm thick. Season with salt.
Dredge in flour, dip in the egg, then lay in the breadcrumbs and coat lightly without pressing (pressing stops the crust puffing).
Heat the fat in a large frying pan to about 170 °C — it should be at least 1.5 cm deep.
Fry the schnitzels one or two at a time, swirling the pan so hot fat washes over the top, until the crust puffs and turns golden (2–3 minutes per side).
Drain on paper and serve immediately with lemon.

recipes.serving: With Viennese potato salad or parsley potatoes and lingonberry jam.
recipes.culture: In Austria, "Wiener Schnitzel" must by law be made with veal; pork versions are called "Schnitzel Wiener Art".

changes: use vegetable oil instead of lard

recipes.title: Anzac Biscuits
recipes.summary: Chewy-crisp oat and coconut biscuits sweetened with golden syrup, baked for Anzac Day.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 160 °C and line two trays with baking paper.
Mix the oats, flour, sugar and coconut in a bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together. Dissolve the soda in the boiling water and stir it into the butter — it will foam.
Pour the foaming mixture into the dry ingredients and mix well.
Roll tablespoons of the mixture into balls and place on the trays, well spaced. Flatten slightly.
Bake until golden. They firm up as they cool — bake longer for crisp, less for chewy.

recipes.culture: Associated with the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps of World War I; the name "Anzac" is protected by law in both countries.

recipes.title: Qutab
recipes.summary: Paper-thin half-moon flatbreads stuffed with a mountain of fresh herbs and greens, cooked on a dry griddle and brushed with butter.
equipment: Large dry frying pan or saj

steps.text: Knead the dough ingredients until smooth, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the greens with the salt, squeeze lightly, and drain off excess liquid. Add the sumac.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and roll each into a very thin 18 cm circle.
Spread a thin layer of filling over half of each circle, fold over and press the edges to seal.
Cook on a hot dry pan for 1–2 minutes per side until speckled brown. Brush generously with butter and stack.

recipes.serving: With yogurt and an extra sprinkle of sumac.

recipes.title: Ćevapi
recipes.summary: Little grilled sausages of seasoned minced beef and lamb, stuffed into fluffy somun bread with raw onion, kajmak and ajvar.

steps.text: Knead the meats with the garlic, soda, salt, pepper and water for 5 minutes until sticky. Cover and chill overnight.
With wet hands, shape into fingers about 2 cm thick and 7 cm long.
Grill over hot coals or on a griddle, turning, until browned and just cooked through (8–10 minutes).
Warm the bread on the grill, split it, and fill with 5–10 ćevapi, onion and kajmak.

recipes.serving: With ajvar (roasted pepper relish) on the side and yogurt to drink.

recipes.title: Cou-Cou
recipes.summary: A smooth, firm cornmeal and okra "pudding" stirred until it holds its shape, traditionally served with flying fish in a spicy Bajan sauce.

items.note: fine yellow cornmeal, mixed with 250 ml cold water
items.name: cornmeal

steps.text: Boil the okra in the salted water until tender.
Lift out the okra with a slotted spoon and keep about half the water in the pot.
Stir the soaked cornmeal into the simmering water and return the okra. Stir constantly with a flat wooden spoon (a cou-cou stick), adding okra water a little at a time.
Keep stirring and turning over low heat until the mixture is smooth and stiff and pulls away from the pot.
Stir in the butter, then shape in a buttered bowl and turn out.

recipes.serving: With steamed flying fish in a tomato, onion and pepper sauce — Barbados's national dish.

recipes.title: Begun Bhorta
recipes.summary: Fire-charred eggplant mashed with pungent mustard oil, raw onion, green chili and cilantro — a smoky Bengali side for rice.

steps.text: Rub the eggplants with a little mustard oil and char them directly over a gas flame, on a grill or under a hot broiler, turning, until the skin is black and the flesh has collapsed.
Let them cool slightly, then peel off the skin and discard the stem. Mash the flesh with a fork or your hand.
Mash in the remaining mustard oil, onion, chili, garlic, cilantro and salt. Taste — it should be smoky, sharp and salty.

tips: Raw mustard oil is the defining flavour; there is no real substitute.
recipes.serving: Hot rice, dal and a selection of other bhortas (mashes) — a classic Bengali lunch.

recipes.title: Carbonade Flamande
recipes.summary: Beef slowly braised in dark Belgian beer with caramelised onions, thickened with a slice of mustard-spread bread.

steps.text: Season the beef and brown it well in batches in the butter. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pot until soft and golden (15 minutes). Stir in the flour.
Return the beef, add the beer, stock, sugar, vinegar, thyme and bay, and bring to a simmer.
Spread the bread with mustard and lay it on top, mustard side down.
Cover and braise very gently, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the bread has melted into the sauce.
Season to taste.

recipes.serving: With Belgian fries and mayonnaise.

recipes.title: Shopska Salad
recipes.summary: Tomatoes, cucumber, peppers and onion under a snowy blanket of finely grated white brined cheese.

steps.text: Combine the vegetables and parsley, dress with oil, vinegar and salt, and toss.
Pile into a bowl and grate the cheese thickly over the top so it covers the salad.

recipes.serving: With a glass of rakia, as a starter.
recipes.culture: Created in the 1950s for Bulgaria's tourism board; its white, green and red echo the Bulgarian flag.

recipes.title: Sopa de Maní
recipes.summary: A creamy soup of blended raw peanuts, beef, potatoes and vegetables, topped with crisp shoestring fries and parsley.

steps.text: Simmer the beef in 2 litres of the water, skimming, until tender.
Blend the peanuts with the remaining 500 ml water until completely smooth.
Fry the onion, garlic, carrot and pepper in the oil until soft, add cumin and oregano, and add to the broth.
Pour in the peanut milk and simmer, stirring often (it catches easily), with the potatoes, peas and pasta until everything is tender.
Meanwhile fry the potato matchsticks until crisp.
Season the soup and serve topped with fries and parsley.

recipes.title: Moqueca Baiana
recipes.summary: Fish stewed in coconut milk with tomatoes, peppers and red dendê palm oil — the signature dish of Bahia.
equipment: heavy pot — traditionally a clay pan

items.note: firm fish such as snapper or halibut
items.name: firm white fish

steps.text: Season the fish with lime juice, garlic and salt and marinate.
In the pot, layer half the onion, peppers, tomato and cilantro. Lay the fish on top, then cover with the remaining vegetables and most of the cilantro.
Pour over the coconut milk and dendê, and add the chili.
Cover and simmer gently without stirring — shake the pan instead — until the fish flakes.
Taste for salt and scatter with the remaining cilantro.

recipes.serving: With white rice, farofa de dendê (toasted cassava flour) and pirão (a fish-broth porridge).
recipes.culture: Afro-Brazilian cuisine in Bahia is built on dendê palm oil, brought by enslaved West Africans along with many of the region's culinary traditions.

recipes.title: Ema Datshi
recipes.summary: Bhutan's national dish — green chilies simmered with onion and tomato in a melting, tangy cheese sauce.

items.note: long green chilies; use milder ones unless you love heat
items.name: fresh green chili

items.note: Bhutanese datshi is a soft cow's-milk cheese; feta mixed with farmer's cheese is a common substitute
items.name: feta

steps.text: Simmer the chilies, onion, garlic and oil in the water.
Add the tomato and cheese and simmer, stirring gently, until the cheese melts into a sauce (about 5 minutes). Don't boil hard.
Season — the cheese is salty, so taste first.

recipes.serving: With Bhutanese red rice.

recipes.title: Seswaa
recipes.summary: Beef boiled slowly with just salt and onion until it falls apart, then pounded into tender shreds — Botswana's national dish.

items.note: on the bone; brisket or chuck also work
items.name: beef shank

steps.text: Put the beef, onion and salt in a heavy pot, cover with water and simmer, topping up the water, until the meat falls off the bone.
Remove the bones. Let most of the liquid evaporate.
Pound and stir the meat with a wooden spoon until it breaks into fine, tender shreds coated in its own juices. Season.

recipes.serving: With pap (stiff maize porridge) and morogo (wild spinach) or beans.
recipes.culture: Traditionally cooked by men in three-legged iron pots and pounded with a wooden pestle at big gatherings.

recipes.title: Poutine
recipes.summary: Crisp double-fried chips topped with squeaky fresh cheese curds and hot, peppery brown gravy.

steps.text: Soak the potato batons in cold water to remove starch, then dry thoroughly.
For the gravy, melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook, stirring, until nut-brown. Whisk in the stock and pepper and simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon. Keep hot.
Fry the potatoes at 160 °C in batches for 5–6 minutes until soft but pale. Drain.
Raise the oil to 190 °C and fry again for 2–3 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain and salt.
Pile the fries into bowls, scatter over the cheese curds, and pour over the hot gravy so the curds just begin to melt.

tips: Fresh curds should squeak against your teeth — don't refrigerate them before using.
recipes.culture: Born in rural Quebec diners in the late 1950s; the name is Quebec slang for "a mess".

changes: use vegetable stock instead of beef stock
use vegetable stock instead of beef stock

recipes.title: Rösti
recipes.summary: A thick, golden potato cake made from coarsely grated parboiled potatoes fried slowly in butter until crisp on both sides.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins until just tender at the edges but firm in the centre. Cool and refrigerate overnight.
Peel and coarsely grate the cold potatoes. Toss with the salt.
Heat half the butter and oil in the pan over medium heat. Add the potatoes and press lightly into a thick cake.
Cook without stirring until a golden crust forms underneath, shaking the pan now and then.
Slide the rösti onto a plate, invert another plate on top and flip. Add the rest of the fat to the pan and slide the rösti back in, uncooked side down.
Cook until crisp and golden.

recipes.serving: As a side for Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal in cream sauce), or topped with a fried egg or melted cheese.
recipes.culture: The "Röstigraben" (rösti ditch) is the jokey name for the cultural border between German- and French-speaking Switzerland.

recipes.title: Alloco
recipes.summary: Sweet ripe plantain cubes fried until caramelised and served with a spicy tomato, onion and chili relish.

items.prep: very ripe, peeled and cut into 2 cm chunks
items.name: plantain

steps.text: Cook the onion in 2 tablespoons oil until soft, add the tomato, chili and salt and cook down to a thick relish (8 minutes).
Heat the frying oil to about 170 °C. Fry the plantain in batches until deep golden and caramelised (3–4 minutes).
Drain, sprinkle with salt and serve with the relish.

recipes.serving: As a street snack, or with grilled fish (poisson braisé) and a boiled egg.

recipes.title: Porotos Granados
recipes.summary: A late-summer stew of fresh shelling beans, squash and grated sweetcorn, scented with basil.

items.note: shelled; or 2 cans cannellini beans, drained
items.name: fresh cranberry beans

items.prep: kernels grated or blended to a coarse purée
items.name: corn on the cob

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil until soft. Add garlic, paprika and oregano and cook 1 minute.
Add the beans, squash and water. Simmer until the beans are tender and the squash begins to fall apart.
Stir in the corn and basil and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Season with salt.

recipes.serving: With pebre (Chilean tomato-chili salsa) or a spoon of ají.

recipes.title: Poulet DG
recipes.summary: Fried chicken and sweet ripe plantains tossed in a colourful sauté of carrots, green beans, peppers and tomato.

items.prep: ripe, peeled and cut into thick rounds
items.name: plantain

steps.text: Season the chicken with the garlic, ginger and salt. Fry it in the hot oil in batches until golden; set aside.
Fry the plantain until caramelised in the same oil; set aside. Pour off all but 3 tablespoons of oil.
Cook the onions in the oil until soft. Add the carrots, beans and peppers and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, Scotch bonnet and chicken. Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables tender.
Fold in the plantain and parsley and heat for 5 minutes.

recipes.culture: Named "Directeur Général" because it was once considered a dish fit for company bosses.

recipes.title: Mapo Tofu
recipes.summary: Soft tofu in a glossy, numbing-hot sauce of fermented broad-bean chili paste, minced beef and Sichuan pepper.

steps.text: Simmer the tofu cubes in lightly salted water for 2 minutes to firm them up. Drain gently.
Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the beef until crisp and browned.
Lower the heat, add the doubanjiang and fry until the oil turns red. Add the black beans, chili, garlic and ginger and fry until fragrant.
Add the stock, soy sauce and sugar, then slide in the tofu. Simmer gently, nudging the tofu with the back of a spoon rather than stirring.
Add the cornstarch slurry in two or three additions until the sauce clings to the tofu.
Serve topped with ground Sichuan pepper and scallion.

recipes.serving: With plenty of steamed rice.
recipes.culture: Said to be named after a pockmarked ("ma") old woman ("po") who served it in a Chengdu restaurant in the 19th century.

recipes.title: Ajiaco
recipes.summary: Bogotá's chicken and three-potato soup, thickened by melting yellow potatoes and scented with the herb guascas, served with cream, capers and avocado.

items.note: half floury, half waxy (sabanera and pastusa)
items.name: potato

items.note: papa criolla; or small Yukon Gold
items.name: yellow potato

items.note: dried; it gives ajiaco its signature flavour
items.name: guascas

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the water with the scallions, garlic and cilantro bunch until cooked.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and discard skin and bones. Discard the scallions and cilantro.
Add the sliced potatoes and the corn to the broth and simmer until the floury potatoes start to fall apart.
Add the papas criollas and guascas and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the criollas dissolve and thicken the soup.
Return the chicken, season with salt and heat through.
Serve in bowls with a piece of corn in each, and cream, capers and avocado for everyone to add at the table.

recipes.serving: With white rice and avocado on the side.

recipes.title: Gallo Pinto
recipes.summary: Day-old rice fried with black beans, onion, pepper, cilantro and tangy Salsa Lizano — the speckled breakfast of Costa Rica.

items.note: 400 g can with about half its liquid
items.name: canned black beans

steps.text: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the oil.
Add the beans with their liquid and the Salsa Lizano and simmer for 3–4 minutes until the liquid reduces slightly.
Add the rice and fold over medium heat until the rice is evenly speckled and heated through.
Stir in the cilantro and season.

recipes.serving: With fried or scrambled eggs, sour cream (natilla), fried sweet plantains and tortillas.
recipes.culture: The name means "spotted rooster". Costa Rica and Nicaragua both claim it as their own.

recipes.title: Cuban Black Beans
recipes.summary: Black beans slowly simmered with a sofrito of onion, green pepper, garlic, cumin and oregano until thick and velvety.

steps.text: Simmer the soaked, drained beans in the water with the bay leaves, partly covered, until soft.
Meanwhile, cook the onion and pepper in the olive oil until soft. Add garlic, cumin and oregano and cook 2 minutes. Add the wine, if using, and let it bubble away.
Stir the sofrito into the beans with the sugar, vinegar and salt. Mash a ladleful of beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
Simmer uncovered until thick and creamy.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.serving: Spooned over white rice (when cooked together, the dish becomes moros y cristianos), with fried plantains.

recipes.title: Cachupa
recipes.summary: Cabo Verde's national dish — a slow stew of hominy corn and beans with pork, sausage, squash, sweet potato and cabbage.

items.note: soaked overnight; a mix of beans is traditional
items.name: dried red kidney beans

steps.text: Drain the hominy and beans and simmer them in the water with the bay leaves. Boil hard for the first 10 minutes.
Add the pork belly and simmer 30 minutes more.
Meanwhile fry the onion and garlic in the oil until soft, add the tomatoes and cook to a sauce; stir it into the pot.
Add the sausage, sweet potato, squash and cabbage, season, and simmer until everything is tender and the stew is thick.

tips: Leftovers are fried the next morning with an egg as cachupa guisada — many say it's even better.
recipes.culture: "Cachupa rica" with plenty of meat is for celebrations; "cachupa pobre" uses only corn, beans and vegetables.

recipes.title: Afelia
recipes.summary: Pork marinated in red wine and crushed coriander seeds, then braised until tender and glossy.

steps.text: Marinate the pork in the wine with half the coriander overnight in the fridge.
Lift out the pork (keep the marinade), pat dry and brown well in the oil.
Add the marinade, cinnamon, bay, the rest of the coriander, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently, stirring now and then, until the pork is tender and the sauce reduced to a glaze.

recipes.serving: With pourgouri (cracked wheat pilaf) or fried potatoes and village salad.

recipes.title: Bramboráky
recipes.summary: Crisp, lacy potato pancakes seasoned with garlic and marjoram, fried in lard until golden.

steps.text: Squeeze the grated potatoes hard in a clean cloth to remove as much liquid as possible.
Mix with the eggs, flour, garlic, marjoram, caraway, salt and pepper.
Heat a thin layer of lard in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Spread spoonfuls of the mixture thinly into pancakes.
Fry until deep golden and crisp, then flip and fry the other side. Add more fat between batches.
Drain on paper and serve hot.

recipes.serving: On their own with beer, or with sauerkraut and roast pork.
