recipes.title: Käsespätzle
recipes.summary: Soft homemade egg noodles layered with melted mountain cheese and topped with sweet, crispy fried onions.
equipment: Spätzle press or a colander with large holes

steps.text: Beat the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg with a wooden spoon until the batter is smooth, thick and forms bubbles. Rest it for 15 minutes.
Fry the onions in 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat until deep brown and crisp (15–20 minutes). Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter through the spätzle press into the water in batches. When the spätzle float, cook 1 minute more and lift out with a slotted spoon.
Layer the hot spätzle and cheese in a buttered ovenproof dish, finishing with cheese.
Bake until the cheese has melted.
Top with the fried onions and chives.

recipes.serving: With a green salad or potato salad.

recipes.title: Frikadeller
recipes.summary: Juicy, flattened pork meatballs fried in butter, served with potatoes, brown gravy and sweet-sour red cabbage.

items.note: or half pork and half veal
items.name: minced pork

steps.text: Mix the pork, onion, egg, flour and seasonings, then work in the milk gradually until the mixture is soft but holds its shape.
Chill so the mixture firms up.
Heat the butter and oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Shape oval patties with a wet tablespoon and the palm of your hand.
Fry, turning once, until browned and cooked through.

recipes.serving: With boiled potatoes, brown gravy, pickled red cabbage (rødkål) or pickled cucumber.

recipes.title: Mangú
recipes.summary: Silky mashed green plantains topped with tangy vinegar-softened red onions — the Dominican breakfast.

steps.text: Boil the plantains in salted water until very tender.
Meanwhile, cook the onions in the oil over medium heat for 2 minutes, add the vinegar and salt and simmer until just soft and pink.
Drain the plantains and immediately mash them with the butter, adding cold water a little at a time until smooth and creamy.
Serve the mangú topped with the onions.

recipes.serving: As "los tres golpes" (the three hits) — with fried Dominican salami, fried cheese and fried eggs.

changes: use vegetable oil instead of butter
use vegetable oil instead of butter

recipes.title: Loubia
recipes.summary: White beans stewed in a garlicky tomato sauce with cumin and paprika — a warming everyday Algerian dish.

steps.text: Soften the onion in the oil, then add the garlic, tomato paste, tomato, paprika, cumin and harissa and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the drained beans, bay leaf and water and simmer, partly covered, until the beans are tender and the sauce is thick.
Season with salt (add it near the end) and finish with cilantro.

recipes.serving: With bread and a drizzle of olive oil; sometimes with a little extra cumin and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.title: Llapingachos
recipes.summary: Golden potato patties stuffed with melting cheese, served with a creamy peanut sauce, fried egg and avocado.

items.note: achiote powder; or paprika for colour
items.name: annatto

steps.text: Boil the potatoes until soft, drain and mash.
Fry the onion in the butter with the annatto until soft, and mix into the potatoes with the salt.
Divide into 8 balls, make a hollow in each, fill with cheese and seal. Flatten into thick patties and chill for 30 minutes.
Fry in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat until golden on both sides.
For the sauce, soften the onion in a little oil, add the milk and peanut butter and simmer, stirring, until smooth and thick.
Serve the patties with the sauce, a fried egg, avocado and lettuce.

recipes.serving: Often with chorizo and curtido (pickled onion and tomato salad).

recipes.title: Mulgipuder
recipes.summary: Potatoes and barley cooked together and mashed, topped with crispy bacon and onion — southern Estonian comfort food.

steps.text: Simmer the barley in the salted water.
Add the potatoes and cook until both are soft.
Drain off most of the water (keep a little) and mash together with the butter into a thick porridge.
Fry the bacon until crisp, add the onion and cook until golden. Spoon over the porridge.

recipes.serving: With a glass of buttermilk or kefir.

recipes.title: Koshari
recipes.summary: Egypt's beloved street food — lentils, rice and pasta layered with spiced tomato sauce, garlic vinegar and crispy onions.

items.note: for frying; the oil is reused below
items.name: vegetable oil

steps.text: Fry the onions in the hot oil over medium heat, stirring, until deep golden and crisp (15–20 minutes). Drain on paper. Keep the oil.
Boil the lentils in plenty of water until just tender but holding their shape (about 20 minutes). Drain.

In a pot, fry the vermicelli in 2 tablespoons of the onion oil until golden. Add the rice, lentils, cumin, salt and 600 ml water. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile cook the macaroni in salted water until al dente. Drain and toss with a spoonful of onion oil.
For the sauce, fry the garlic in 2 tablespoons of onion oil for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, vinegar, cumin, chili and salt, and simmer until thickened.
Stir the dakka ingredients together with a pinch of salt.
Warm the chickpeas. To serve, layer rice-lentil mix, then macaroni, then sauce, chickpeas and a heap of crispy onions. Let everyone add dakka to taste.

tips: The onion oil is the secret — it seasons every layer.
recipes.serving: In deep bowls, with extra sauce and dakka on the side.
recipes.culture: Koshari became a working-class staple in the 19th century; it is commonly linked to Indian kitchari and Italian pasta, which both reached Egypt in that era.

recipes.title: Tsebhi Zigni
recipes.summary: Tender beef in a deep, spicy berbere and onion sauce — Eritrea's most celebrated stew, eaten with injera.

steps.text: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium heat, stirring, until soft and lightly coloured.
Add the oil and berbere and cook, stirring and adding splashes of water, for 10 minutes until dark red and fragrant.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and tomato and cook 5 minutes.
Add the beef and water. Cover and simmer gently until the beef is tender and the sauce thick.
Stir in the cardamom and season.

recipes.serving: On injera, often with a hard-boiled egg added to the sauce for special occasions.

recipes.title: Spanish Potato Omelette
recipes.summary: A thick, golden omelette of potatoes and onion slowly poached in olive oil, with a soft, just-set centre.
equipment: A plate wider than the pan

items.note: "con cebolla" or "sin cebolla" — a national debate
items.name: onion

items.note: most of it is drained off and can be reused
items.name: olive oil

steps.text: Heat the oil in the pan over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes and onion with a pinch of salt and cook gently, turning now and then, until completely tender but barely coloured.
Drain the potatoes in a sieve over a bowl (keep the oil).
Beat the eggs with the salt in a large bowl. Add the hot potatoes, press them under the egg and leave so the potatoes absorb some of it.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in the pan over medium heat. Pour in the mixture and shape the sides with a spatula. Cook for 3–4 minutes until the bottom is set.
Put a plate over the pan and turn it over confidently in one movement. Slide the tortilla back in, uncooked side down, and cook 2–3 minutes more. The centre should still be slightly soft.

recipes.serving: Warm or at room temperature, in wedges or cubes as a tapa, or in a baguette as a bocadillo.

recipes.title: Misir Wot
recipes.summary: Red lentils simmered with slow-cooked onions and berbere spice — a fiery, everyday Ethiopian stew eaten with injera.

items.note: oil on fasting days; niter kibbeh otherwise
items.name: vegetable oil

steps.text: Cook the onions in a dry pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, until soft and starting to colour. Add a splash of water if they catch.
Add the oil and cook the onions a few minutes more, then stir in the berbere, garlic, ginger and tomato paste, if using. Cook for 3 minutes, adding a little water if the spices start to stick.
Add the lentils and water. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the lentils collapse into a thick stew. Add more water if it gets too stiff.
Season with salt and serve hot.

tips: Cooking the onions without fat first is a hallmark of Ethiopian stews; it gives a sweeter, deeper base.
recipes.serving: Spooned onto injera with other wots and vegetable dishes, eaten by hand.
recipes.culture: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians fast from animal products on Wednesdays, Fridays and through Lent, so misir wot made with oil is a staple of the fasting table.

recipes.title: Lohikeitto
recipes.summary: A gentle, creamy soup of salmon, potatoes and leek, seasoned with allspice and plenty of dill.

steps.text: Soften the leek in the butter for 3 minutes.
Add the potatoes, carrot, water, allspice, bay and salt and simmer until the potatoes are just tender.
Add the cream and salmon and simmer very gently — don't boil — until the salmon is just cooked.
Stir in most of the dill and serve with the rest on top.

recipes.serving: With rye bread and butter.

recipes.title: Kokoda
recipes.summary: Fijian raw fish cured in citrus and dressed in fresh coconut cream with chili, tomato and onion.

steps.text: Toss the fish with salt and lime juice. Cover and refrigerate, stirring once, until the fish is opaque all the way through.
Drain off most of the juice.
Stir in the coconut cream, onion, tomato, cucumber, chili and scallion. Taste for salt and serve cold.

tips: Use fish labelled for raw consumption or previously frozen fish.
recipes.serving: In a coconut shell or a halved coconut, with cassava or taro on the side.

recipes.title: Ratatouille
recipes.summary: Provençal summer vegetables — aubergine, courgette, peppers and tomato — each cooked separately in olive oil then gently stewed together with herbs.

steps.text: Fry the aubergine in 2 tablespoons oil until golden; set aside. Do the same with the courgette, then the peppers, adding oil as needed. Season each batch lightly.
In the same pot, soften the onion in the remaining oil, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, thyme and bay and cook for 10 minutes until saucy.
Return all the vegetables, stir gently, cover and stew over low heat.
Stir in the basil, season, and serve hot, warm or cold.

tips: It is better the next day.
recipes.serving: As a side for grilled meat or fish, with rice, or on its own with bread and an egg.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.summary: Minced lamb slowly cooked with vegetables in a rich gravy, under a thick, golden layer of mashed potato.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil in batches over high heat. Remove and pour off excess fat.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the same pan for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, flour and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Return the lamb, add the Worcestershire sauce, stock and thyme, and simmer until thick and rich.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes until tender, drain well and mash with butter, milk and seasoning. Heat the oven to 200 °C.
Spread the filling in the dish, cover with mash and rough up the top with a fork. Sprinkle over the cheese, if using.
Bake until bubbling and the top is golden.

tips: Made with minced beef, it's called cottage pie.
recipes.serving: With peas or buttered greens.

recipes.title: Lobio
recipes.summary: Red kidney beans stewed until creamy and seasoned Georgian-style with onion, garlic, cilantro, coriander and khmeli suneli.

steps.text: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water and boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer until very soft.
Meanwhile fry the onions in the oil until golden.
Mash about half of the beans in their pot with a potato masher, keeping the rest whole. It should be thick but loose; add water if needed.
Stir in the onions, garlic, spices, walnuts, vinegar and most of the cilantro. Season with salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Finish with the remaining cilantro.

recipes.serving: Hot in a clay pot (lobio kotanshi) with mchadi (corn bread), pickled vegetables and fresh herbs.

recipes.title: Red-Red
recipes.summary: Black-eyed peas stewed in red palm oil with tomato and chili, served with sweet fried ripe plantain.

items.note: 400 g cans, drained; or 300 g dried, soaked and boiled
items.name: black-eyed peas

items.prep: very ripe (mostly black), peeled and sliced on the diagonal
items.name: plantain

steps.text: Warm the palm oil in a pot over medium heat (don't let it smoke). Fry the onion until soft, then add garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook down, stirring, until thick and the oil separates.
Add the beans, smoked fish if using, water and salt. Simmer, stirring gently, until thick and the beans are soft enough to mash slightly.
Meanwhile, sprinkle the plantain with salt and shallow-fry in the vegetable oil in batches until caramelised on both sides. Drain on paper.
Serve the beans with the plantain alongside.

tips: Red palm oil gives the dish its colour and name; vegetable oil plus a teaspoon of paprika is a reasonable substitute.
recipes.serving: Often with gari (toasted cassava) sprinkled on top.
recipes.culture: The name comes from its two red parts — beans in red palm oil and orange-red fried plantain.

recipes.title: Domoda
recipes.summary: Beef stewed in a rich, tomato-red peanut sauce with squash and Scotch bonnet — the Gambia's national dish.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil. Add the onions and garlic and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the water, cover and simmer until the beef is nearly tender.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of broth until smooth and stir it in, with the squash, Scotch bonnet and bouillon.
Simmer, stirring often, until the squash is soft and oil glistens on the surface.
Season and remove the Scotch bonnet before serving.

recipes.serving: Over white rice.

recipes.title: Fasolada
recipes.summary: White beans simmered with carrot, celery and tomato in plenty of good olive oil, finished with lemon.

steps.text: Soak the beans overnight in plenty of cold water.
Drain the beans, cover with fresh water, bring to a boil for 5 minutes and drain again.
Heat half the oil in a large pot and soften the onion, carrot, celery and garlic for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste.
Add the beans, tomatoes, bay leaves and water. Simmer, partly covered, until the beans are creamy.
Add salt only now (it toughens beans if added early) and the rest of the olive oil. Simmer 10 minutes more.

recipes.serving: With lemon, bread, olives, feta (if not fasting), and raw onion or pickled fish on the side.
recipes.culture: Often called Greece's national dish; a staple of the Orthodox fasting days when meat and dairy are avoided.

recipes.title: Pepián de Pollo
recipes.summary: Chicken and vegetables in a thick, smoky sauce of toasted tomatoes, dried chilies, pumpkin and sesame seeds — Guatemala's national dish.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken in the salted water until just cooked. Keep the broth.
On a dry pan, char the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, garlic and pepper until blackened in spots.
Separately toast the chilies for a few seconds, then the pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds and cinnamon until golden — watch they don't burn.
Blend everything for the recado with the tortilla and 500 ml of broth until smooth.
Strain the sauce into a pot, add the potatoes and chayote and simmer until nearly tender, adding broth to keep it thick but pourable.
Add the chicken and green beans and simmer until heated through and the beans are tender.
Finish with cilantro and season.

recipes.serving: With white rice and corn tortillas or tamalitos.
recipes.culture: A Maya-Spanish mestizo dish; it was declared part of Guatemala's intangible cultural heritage in 2007.

recipes.title: Baleadas
recipes.summary: Thick, soft flour tortillas folded around refried red beans, crumbled salty cheese and Honduran cream.

steps.text: Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, rub in the fat, then add the water and knead into a soft dough. Divide into 8 balls and rest 30 minutes.
Stretch each ball by hand (or roll) into a thin 20 cm round.
Cook on a hot dry griddle for 1 minute per side until puffed and spotted.
Spread with warm beans, sprinkle with cheese and drizzle with cream. Add egg or avocado if you like, and fold in half.

recipes.title: Brudet
recipes.summary: Mixed fish slowly simmered in olive oil, onion, tomato and wine — never stirred, only shaken — and served with polenta.

items.note: mixed steaks — e.g. monkfish, grouper, scorpion fish
items.name: firm white fish

steps.text: Soften the onions in the oil in a wide pot, add the garlic and tomato paste, then the tomatoes, wine, vinegar and bay.
Simmer to a sauce.
Lay the fish in the sauce in one layer, season and add water to almost cover.
Simmer gently with the lid ajar. Don't stir — shake the pot from time to time so nothing sticks or breaks.
Meanwhile, cook the polenta by whisking the cornmeal into the salted boiling water and stirring over low heat until thick.
Scatter the brudet with parsley and serve with the polenta.

recipes.title: Soup Joumou
recipes.summary: A rich squash soup with beef, vegetables and pasta, eaten by Haitians every 1 January to celebrate independence.

steps.text: Blend the epis ingredients to a coarse paste.
Toss the beef with half the epis and 1 teaspoon salt and marinate.
Put the beef and 1 litre of water in the pot and simmer, covered, until the beef is nearly tender.
Meanwhile simmer the squash in 1 litre of water until soft, then blend it with its cooking water until smooth.
Add the squash purée, the remaining water and epis, onion, celery, carrot, potato, cabbage, cloves and Scotch bonnet to the beef.
Simmer until all the vegetables are tender.
Add the pasta and cook until tender, adding water if the soup is too thick. Remove the Scotch bonnet, season with salt and stir in the butter.

recipes.culture: Under French colonial rule, enslaved Haitians grew squash but were forbidden to eat this soup. After independence on 1 January 1804, eating soup joumou became a celebration of freedom. It was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2021.

recipes.title: Chicken Paprikash
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in a rich onion and sweet paprika sauce, finished with sour cream.

items.prep: bone-in pieces, skin removed if you like
items.name: chicken thigh

steps.text: Melt the lard and cook the onions slowly until soft and golden.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika — it burns easily and turns bitter.
Immediately add the chicken, tomato, pepper, water and salt. Return to the heat.
Cover and simmer, turning the chicken occasionally, until tender.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour and a ladle of hot sauce, then stir it into the pot. Simmer gently for 3 minutes without boiling hard.

recipes.serving: With nokedli (small egg dumplings) or buttered noodles, and cucumber salad.

changes: use vegetable oil instead of lard

recipes.title: Nasi Goreng
recipes.summary: Indonesia's national fried rice — day-old rice fried with a chili-shallot paste, shrimp paste and sweet soy, topped with a fried egg.
equipment: Mortar and pestle or small blender

steps.text: Pound or blend the spice-paste ingredients to a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the paste until fragrant and darker (2–3 minutes).
Add the chicken, if using, and stir-fry until cooked.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and toss over high heat for 3–4 minutes. Add kecap manis and salt and toss until every grain is coloured.
Serve topped with a fried egg, with cucumber, tomato, fried shallots and crackers on the side.

recipes.title: Brown Soda Bread
recipes.summary: A rustic wholemeal loaf leavened with baking soda and buttermilk instead of yeast — mixed in minutes, with no kneading or rising.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C and dust a baking tray with flour.
Mix the flours, soda and salt in a large bowl. Make a well and pour in most of the buttermilk.
Mix quickly with your hand or a spoon into a soft, slightly sticky dough, adding the rest of the buttermilk if dry. Don't knead — handle as little as possible.
Shape into a round about 4 cm high on the tray. Cut a deep cross on top.
Bake until the loaf sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
Wrap in a clean tea towel to cool, which keeps the crust soft.

recipes.culture: The cross is said to "let the fairies out" — and helps the thick loaf bake through.

recipes.title: Chana Masala
recipes.summary: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy, deeply spiced onion-tomato gravy — a North Indian staple.

items.note: 400 g cans, drained (keep a little liquid)
items.name: canned chickpeas

steps.text: Heat the oil and add cumin seeds and bay leaf. When the seeds sizzle, add the onion.
Fry the onion until deep golden brown — this gives the gravy its colour.
Add ginger, garlic and chili and fry 1 minute. Add the ground spices with a splash of water and fry for 1 minute more.
Add the tomatoes and cook until the masala thickens and oil appears around the edges.
Add the chickpeas, water and salt. Simmer, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Stir in garam masala and amchur, and finish with cilantro.

recipes.serving: With bhature (fried bread), rice or roti, sliced raw onion and lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Timman Bagilla
alternate_names: Iraqi dill and broad bean rice
recipes.summary: Basmati rice layered with broad beans and lots of dill, often served with slow-cooked lamb.

steps.text: If using lamb, simmer it with the water, cardamom, dried lime and bay leaves until very tender. Keep the broth.
Rinse the rice and soak it.
Fry the broad beans in the oil for 3 minutes, add the drained rice, dill, turmeric and salt and stir to coat.
Add 650 ml of broth or water, bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat until fluffy.
Serve the rice topped with the lamb.

recipes.serving: With yogurt and a tomato-cucumber salad.

recipes.title: Kuku Sabzi
recipes.summary: A thick, vivid-green frittata that is mostly fresh herbs, studded with walnuts and tart barberries.
equipment: 24 cm non-stick pan with a lid

steps.text: Wash and dry the herbs very well, discard the thick stems, and chop finely — you want about 4 packed cups.
Whisk the eggs with turmeric, baking powder, flour, salt and pepper. Fold in the herbs, fenugreek, walnuts and barberries. The mixture should be more green than yellow.
Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat, pour in the mixture and smooth the top.
Cover and cook on low until the bottom is set and browned.
Cut into quarters and flip each one (or flip the whole kuku onto a plate and slide it back). Cook uncovered for 10 minutes more. Alternatively, bake the whole thing at 180 °C for 30 minutes.

recipes.serving: Warm or at room temperature with flatbread, yogurt and pickles.
recipes.culture: Eaten at Nowruz, the Persian New Year, when the green herbs symbolise rebirth and spring.

recipes.title: Plokkfiskur
recipes.summary: Flaked white fish and potatoes folded into a peppery white sauce — Icelandic home cooking at its most comforting.

steps.text: Poach the fish in barely simmering salted water until it just flakes. Drain and flake, removing any bones.
Soften the onion in the butter, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and simmer until thick.
Roughly chop the potatoes and fold them and the fish into the sauce. Season generously with pepper — it should be chunky, not smooth.

recipes.serving: With dark, sweet rye bread (rúgbrauð) and butter.

recipes.title: Cacio e Pepe
recipes.summary: Roman pasta with only three ingredients — pecorino, black pepper and starchy pasta water whipped into a creamy sauce.

items.note: for the pasta water — use less than usual, the cheese is salty
items.name: salt

steps.text: Cook the pasta in a smaller amount of water than usual (about 2 litres) so it gets very starchy. Lightly salt it.
Toast the pepper in a large dry frying pan for 1 minute, then add a ladle of pasta water and let it simmer.
In a bowl, mash the pecorino with a few spoonfuls of lukewarm (not hot) pasta water into a thick, smooth paste.
Two minutes before the pasta is al dente, transfer it to the pepper pan with tongs and finish cooking it there, adding pasta water as needed.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 30 seconds. Add the cheese paste and toss vigorously, adding splashes of water until the sauce is creamy and coats the pasta. Serve immediately.

tips: If the pan is too hot the cheese turns into clumps; off the heat and lukewarm water are the keys.
recipes.culture: A dish of Roman shepherds, who carried dried pasta, aged pecorino and pepper because none of them spoil.

recipes.title: Rice and Peas
recipes.summary: Rice cooked with kidney beans in coconut milk, fragrant with thyme, scallion, allspice and a whole Scotch bonnet.

items.note: whole and unbroken — for aroma, not heat
items.name: Scotch bonnet chili

steps.text: Bring the beans with their liquid, coconut milk, water, garlic, scallion, thyme, allspice, Scotch bonnet and salt to a boil.
Stir in the rice. The liquid should cover the rice by about 1.5 cm; add water if needed.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Remove the scallion, thyme and the whole pepper (carefully — don't burst it). Fluff and serve.

tips: In Jamaica "peas" means kidney beans; pigeon peas (gungo peas) are used at Christmas.
recipes.serving: With curry goat, brown stew chicken or jerk chicken.

recipes.title: Galayet Bandora
recipes.summary: Ripe tomatoes fried down in olive oil with garlic and hot green chili until jammy — a quick, rustic dish scooped up with bread.

steps.text: Fry the onion (if using), garlic and chili in the olive oil until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook over medium-high heat, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse into a thick, glossy stew.
Top with pine nuts and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.serving: From the pan, with warm flatbread and olives.

recipes.title: Oyakodon
recipes.summary: Chicken and onion simmered in sweet-savoury dashi, bound with softly set egg and slid over a bowl of rice.
equipment: Small frying pan with a lid (an oyakodon pan if you have one)

items.prep: lightly beaten — leave streaks of white
items.name: egg

steps.text: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar in the pan. Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken in a single layer and simmer, turning once, until cooked through.

Pour two-thirds of the egg over the chicken. Cover and cook for 1 minute, then pour over the rest of the egg, cover and turn off the heat. Leave for 30–60 seconds — the top should still be soft and glossy.
Slide half the mixture over each bowl of rice with some of the broth, and top with scallion.

tips: Cook one portion at a time in a small pan for the best texture.
recipes.culture: The name means "parent-and-child bowl" — chicken and egg in one dish.

recipes.title: Sukuma Wiki with Ugali
recipes.summary: Collard greens sautéed with onion and tomato, eaten with ugali — a firm, smooth maize-flour staple.

items.note: fine white maize meal; not cornstarch
items.name: white maize flour

items.prep: stems removed, leaves rolled and very thinly sliced
items.name: collard greens

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy pot. Sprinkle in a third of the maize flour, stirring, and cook to a thin porridge for 2 minutes.
Add the rest of the flour gradually, pressing and folding with a sturdy wooden spoon against the side of the pot, until stiff and smooth with no dry lumps.
Reduce the heat and keep turning and pressing the ugali until it smells toasty and pulls away from the pot. Shape into a dome and cover.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onion until soft. Add the tomato and cook until it collapses.
Add the greens and salt and stir-fry just until wilted and bright green (3–5 minutes).

tips: Kale works in place of collards.
recipes.serving: Pinch off a piece of ugali, press a dent into it with your thumb, and use it to scoop the greens. Often served with nyama choma (grilled meat) or stew.
recipes.culture: Sukuma wiki means "push the week" in Swahili — cheap greens that stretch the household budget to payday.

recipes.title: Beef Lok Lak
recipes.summary: Seared marinated beef cubes on fresh lettuce, tomato and onion, with a punchy Kampot-pepper and lime dipping sauce.

steps.text: Toss the beef with the oyster sauce, soy, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and pepper and marinate.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato, onion and cucumber on plates.
Heat the oil in a wok until smoking and sear the beef in a single layer, tossing once, until browned outside and pink inside (2–3 minutes).
Pile the beef onto the salad. Mix the pepper, salt and lime juice in small bowls for dipping.

recipes.serving: With rice and a fried egg on top.

recipes.title: Kimchi Jjigae
recipes.summary: A bubbling, sour-spicy stew of well-fermented kimchi, pork belly and tofu — Korean comfort food.

steps.text: In a pot, fry the pork belly over medium heat until it renders some fat and starts to brown.
Add the kimchi and stir-fry with the pork for 5 minutes until it softens and smells toasty.
Add onion, garlic, gochugaru, gochujang, sugar, kimchi juice and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer, partly covered, until the kimchi is tender and the broth is rich.
Lay the tofu on top and simmer 5 minutes more. Add the scallion and sesame oil and serve bubbling.

tips: Old, very sour kimchi makes the best jjigae.
Omit the pork and use vegan kimchi and kelp stock for a vegan version.
recipes.serving: In the pot, in the middle of the table, with rice and banchan.

recipes.title: Beshbarmak
recipes.summary: Slow-simmered meat over sheets of fresh noodles, topped with onions softened in the rich broth, which is drunk alongside.

items.note: on the bone; horse meat or lamb are traditional too
items.name: beef shank

steps.text: Cover the meat with the water, bring to a boil and skim well. Add the whole onion, bay, peppercorns and salt and simmer gently until the meat is very tender.
Meanwhile mix the noodle ingredients into a stiff dough, knead until smooth and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin (about 1 mm) and cut into 7 cm squares.
Lift out the meat and cut it into pieces. Put the onion rings in a bowl with the pepper and pour over a ladle of hot fat-rich broth; cover.
Boil the noodle squares in batches in the broth for 2–3 minutes and lift onto a large platter.
Pile the meat on the noodles and top with the onions. Serve the remaining broth (sorpa) in bowls.

recipes.culture: The name means "five fingers" — it was traditionally eaten by hand.

recipes.title: Larb
recipes.summary: Minced chicken tossed warm with lime, fish sauce, chili, toasted rice powder and lots of fresh herbs — Laos's national dish.

steps.text: Toast the rice in a dry pan, shaking, until deep golden (about 5 minutes). Grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the chicken with the water in a pan over medium heat, breaking it up, until just cooked through. Take off the heat.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and chili, then the shallots, scallion, herbs and 1 tablespoon of the rice powder.
Taste — it should be sour, salty and hot. Sprinkle with more rice powder and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.serving: With sticky rice, eaten by hand, and raw vegetables such as cabbage wedges and long beans.

recipes.title: Tabbouleh
recipes.summary: A bright, herb-heavy salad of finely chopped parsley and mint with a little bulgur, tomato and plenty of lemon.

items.note: flat-leaf, about 150 g leaves, very finely chopped
items.name: flat-leaf parsley

steps.text: Rinse the bulgur, then soak it in the lemon juice until softened.
Wash the parsley and dry it completely, then chop it finely with a sharp knife (a food processor bruises it).
Combine everything just before serving and season generously with salt. It should taste green, lemony and sharp.

tips: In Lebanon, tabbouleh is mostly parsley — the bulgur is a sprinkle, not a base.
recipes.serving: As part of a mezze spread, scooped up with crisp lettuce or cabbage leaves.

changes: use quinoa instead of fine bulgur

recipes.title: Parippu
recipes.summary: Red lentils simmered in coconut milk with turmeric, then finished with a sizzling tempering of mustard seeds, curry leaves and chili.

steps.text: Simmer the lentils, water, onion, garlic, chili, turmeric and pandan until the lentils are soft and breaking up.
Stir in the coconut milk and salt and simmer 5 minutes more. Add water if you want it thinner.
Heat the coconut oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds; when they pop, add cumin, dried chili, curry leaves and sliced onion. Fry until the onion is golden.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the dhal and stir.

recipes.serving: With rice and other curries, or with roti or string hoppers for breakfast.

recipes.title: Šaltibarščiai
recipes.summary: A bright pink cold soup of kefir, beetroot, cucumber, dill and egg, served with hot boiled potatoes on the side.

items.note: cooked and peeled, then grated or cut into matchsticks
items.name: beetroot

steps.text: Mix the kefir, beetroot, cucumber, most of the dill, scallions and salt. Thin with a little cold water if very thick. Chill.
Chop two eggs into the soup; halve the others for the top.
Serve cold, garnished with egg and dill, with hot potatoes on the side.

recipes.title: Judd mat Gaardebounen
alternate_names: Smoked pork collar with broad beans
recipes.summary: Luxembourg's national dish — smoked pork collar simmered until tender, with broad beans in a creamy savory-scented sauce.

steps.text: Drain the pork, cover with fresh water, add the vegetables and spices, and simmer very gently until tender.
Boil the beans in salted water until tender (5–8 minutes). Drain, keeping 300 ml of the water.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the bean water and a ladle of the pork broth and simmer until thick. Add the cream, savory and beans and season.
Slice the pork and serve with the beans and potatoes.

recipes.serving: With a Luxembourg Moselle wine or local beer.

recipes.title: Grey Peas with Bacon
recipes.summary: Earthy grey peas tossed with crisp smoked bacon and onion — a Latvian national dish, essential at Christmas.

steps.text: Drain the peas, cover with fresh water and simmer until tender but not mushy. Drain.
Fry the bacon until it renders and crisps. Add the onion and cook until golden.
Toss the peas with the bacon, onion and fat, season and serve hot.

recipes.serving: With a glass of kefir.

recipes.title: Shorba Libiya
recipes.summary: A spiced tomato soup with lamb, chickpeas and tiny orzo pasta, finished with dried mint — the dish that breaks the fast in Ramadan.

steps.text: Brown the lamb in the oil, then add the onion and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and spices and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the water and simmer, covered, until the lamb is tender.
Add the chickpeas and orzo and cook until the pasta is soft, stirring so it doesn't stick.
Rub the dried mint between your palms into the soup, add the parsley and season.

recipes.serving: With lemon wedges and bread, before the main iftar meal.

recipes.title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.summary: Chicken braised with ginger, saffron and onions until tender, finished with salty preserved lemon and olives.

items.prep: pulp discarded, peel cut into strips
items.name: preserved lemon

items.note: to taste — the lemon and olives are salty
items.name: salt

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the onion, garlic, spices, saffron water, oil and half the herbs. Leave to marinate.
Tip everything into the tagine or pot, add the water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat, turning the chicken once or twice, until it is very tender.
Add the preserved lemon and olives and cook uncovered for 10–15 minutes until the sauce thickens. Taste before adding salt.
Scatter over the remaining herbs and serve from the pot.

tips: The marinade can sit overnight in the fridge for deeper flavour.
A clay tagine needs a heat diffuser on gas or electric hobs.
recipes.serving: With khobz (Moroccan round bread) to scoop up the sauce.

recipes.title: Romazava
recipes.summary: Madagascar's national dish — a gingery beef and greens broth made tingly by brèdes mafana (paracress).

items.note: brèdes mafana; watercress plus a little extra ginger is the usual substitute
items.name: paracress

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes, water and salt and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add the greens and simmer until wilted and tender.
Taste for salt; the broth should be clear and gingery.

recipes.serving: Spooned over plenty of white rice, with sakay (chili paste) on the side.

recipes.title: Tavče Gravče
recipes.summary: North Macedonia's national dish — white beans cooked with onion, paprika and dried chili, then baked in a clay dish until crusted.

items.note: soaked overnight; Tetovo beans are the classic
items.name: dried white beans

steps.text: Simmer the drained beans in the water until tender, keeping them covered with liquid.
Fry the onions in the oil until soft. Stir in the flour, then the paprika off the heat.
Stir the onion mixture, chilies, mint, salt and pepper into the beans with enough liquid to keep them saucy, and pour into the dish.
Bake at 200 °C until bubbling with a browned top.

recipes.serving: With crusty bread and pickled peppers.

recipes.title: Mohinga

native_name.text: မုန့်ဟင်းခါး

recipes.summary: Rice noodles in a rich, lemongrass-scented fish broth thickened with toasted chickpea flour — Myanmar's national breakfast.

items.prep: toasted in a dry pan until golden
items.name: chickpea flour

steps.text: Simmer the fish in the water with the bruised lemongrass and turmeric until cooked. Lift out the fish and flake it, discarding bones. Keep the broth.
Pound or blend the shallots, garlic, ginger and lemongrass to a paste. Fry it in the oil with the paprika and chili until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the flaked fish to the paste and fry for 5 minutes.
Whisk the toasted chickpea flour and rice powder with a ladle of broth until smooth, then stir it into the broth.
Add the fish mixture and fish sauce and simmer, stirring often, until thickened and rich.
Put noodles in bowls, ladle over the soup and top with egg, fried shallots, cilantro, lime and chili.

tips: Slices of banana stem are traditional in the broth if you can find them.

recipes.title: Buuz
recipes.summary: Steamed dumplings packed with juicy minced mutton, onion and garlic — Mongolia's essential Lunar New Year food.

items.note: fatty mutton is traditional; beef also works
items.name: minced lamb

steps.text: Knead the dough ingredients until smooth; rest 20 minutes.
Mix the filling ingredients thoroughly.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 30 pieces and roll each into a 7 cm round.
Put a spoonful of filling in the centre and pleat the edges up around it, leaving a small opening at the top.
Steam over boiling water until the filling is cooked through.

recipes.serving: With pickled vegetables or salad, and milk tea (suutei tsai). Eat carefully — the juice inside is hot.
recipes.culture: Families make hundreds or thousands of buuz together in the days before Tsagaan Sar and freeze them for guests.

recipes.title: Stuffat tal-Fenek
recipes.summary: Rabbit marinated in red wine and garlic, then slowly stewed with tomatoes, peas and potatoes — Malta's national dish.

steps.text: Marinate the rabbit in the wine, garlic and bay overnight in the fridge.
Lift out the rabbit (keep the marinade), pat dry and brown it in the oil. Set aside.
Soften the onions in the same pot, add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute.
Return the rabbit with the marinade and tomatoes, cover and simmer gently.
Add the potatoes and peas and cook until tender.
Season. The sauce is traditionally eaten first with spaghetti, followed by the rabbit as a main course.

recipes.title: Rougaille Saucisse
recipes.summary: Sausages simmered in a fragrant Creole tomato sauce with ginger, garlic, thyme and green chili.

steps.text: Brown the sausages lightly in the oil; set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pan until soft, then add garlic, ginger and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chilies and cook down until thick and jammy.
Return the sausages, season and simmer to blend the flavours.
Finish with scallion and cilantro.

recipes.serving: With rice, lentils (dal) and chutneys.

changes: use shrimp instead of smoked sausage
use shrimp instead of smoked sausage

recipes.title: Mas Huni
recipes.summary: Tuna mixed with fresh grated coconut, onion, chili and lime — the classic Maldivian breakfast, rolled up in warm roshi.

items.note: drained (about 300 g); smoked tuna is traditional
items.name: canned tuna

items.note: or freshly grated coconut; soak desiccated in 4 tbsp warm water
items.name: desiccated coconut

steps.text: Rub the onion, chili and salt together with your fingers to release their juices.
Add the tuna, coconut and lime juice and mix by hand until evenly combined.

recipes.serving: With roshi (thin flatbread) and sweet black tea.

recipes.title: Chambo with Nsima
recipes.summary: Whole tilapia from Lake Malawi, fried crisp and served with a fresh tomato and onion relish and soft nsima.

items.note: whole, scaled and gutted (about 400 g each)
items.name: tilapia

items.note: cooked as for ugali (see the Kenyan recipe)
items.name: white maize flour

steps.text: Slash the fish on both sides and rub with lemon juice and salt.
Pat dry and fry in hot oil, about 6 minutes per side, until crisp and cooked through.
For the relish, fry the onion until soft, add the tomatoes, chili and salt, and simmer for 8 minutes.
Serve the fish with the relish and nsima.

recipes.title: Chilaquiles Rojos
recipes.summary: Crisp-fried tortilla wedges tossed in a smoky guajillo and tomato salsa, topped with crumbled cheese, crema, onion and a fried egg.

items.note: a day old, each cut into 6 wedges
items.name: corn tortilla

steps.text: Fry the tortilla wedges in hot oil in batches until golden and crisp. Drain on paper and sprinkle with salt. (Or use good thick store-bought totopos.)
Toast the dried chilies in a dry pan for a few seconds per side until fragrant, then soak in hot water for 10 minutes.
Boil the tomatoes, onion and garlic in water for 10 minutes. Blend with the drained chilies and a little cooking water until smooth.
Fry the salsa in the oil in a wide pan, stirring, until it darkens and thickens slightly. Season with salt.
Add the totopos and toss to coat. Serve immediately (crunchy) or after a minute (softer) — it's a matter of taste.
Top with cheese, crema, onion, cilantro, a fried egg and avocado.

recipes.serving: With refried beans on the side. A favourite breakfast and hangover cure.

recipes.title: Nasi Lemak
recipes.summary: Fragrant coconut-pandan rice with sweet-hot sambal, crispy anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber — Malaysia's national breakfast.

items.prep: soaked in hot water 20 minutes, deseeded
items.name: dried red chili

steps.text: Put all the coconut-rice ingredients in a pot or rice cooker. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on very low heat for 15 minutes. Rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Blend the soaked chilies, shallots, garlic and shrimp paste to a smooth paste with a splash of water.
Fry the paste in the 6 tablespoons oil over medium-low heat, stirring often, until it darkens and the oil separates. This is slow — don't rush it.
Add the onion rings, tamarind, sugar and salt and cook 5 minutes more until jammy. The sambal should be sweet, sour and hot.
Fry the anchovies in the 100 ml oil until crisp and golden; drain.
Serve a mound of rice with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber around it.

recipes.serving: Traditionally wrapped in a banana leaf, often with fried chicken or rendang added.

recipes.title: Piri-Piri Chicken
recipes.summary: Spatchcocked chicken marinated in a fiery bird's-eye chili, garlic and lemon sauce and grilled over coals.

steps.text: Blend the sauce ingredients until smooth. Keep a quarter aside for basting and serving.
Slash the chicken through the thickest parts and rub with the remaining sauce. Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Grill skin-side up over medium coals with the lid closed, basting occasionally, then flip and crisp the skin. Or roast at 200 °C. The thickest part of the thigh should reach 74 °C.
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut into pieces and serve with the reserved sauce.

recipes.serving: With chips, rice or bread rolls and a tomato-onion salad.
recipes.culture: Bird's-eye chilies of African origin met Portuguese cooking in colonial Mozambique and Angola; the dish was later popularised worldwide by Portuguese and South African restaurants.

recipes.title: Kapana
recipes.summary: Strips of beef grilled fast over coals and dipped in a hot spice mix, eaten straight off the grill with tomato-chili salsa.

steps.text: Mix the spice-dip ingredients in a small bowl. Mix the salsa ingredients with a pinch of salt.
Toss the beef with the oil and salt and grill over very hot coals or a smoking griddle for 1–2 minutes per side.
Cut into bite-size pieces and serve with the spice dip and salsa.

recipes.culture: Named after the Oshiwambo word for the spice dip, kapana is sold sizzling from open grills in markets such as Windhoek's Single Quarters.

recipes.title: Jollof Rice
recipes.summary: Long-grain rice cooked in a deep-red, smoky reduction of peppers, tomatoes and onion — the centrepiece of West African parties.
equipment: Heavy pot with a tight lid

items.prep: rinsed until the water runs clear
items.name: parboiled long-grain rice

steps.text: Blend the pepper-base ingredients until smooth.
Pour the blend into a pot and boil uncovered, stirring now and then, until reduced by about half and thick.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion until soft, then add the tomato paste and fry, stirring, until it darkens a shade (about 5 minutes).
Add the reduced pepper base, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves and the crumbled bouillon cube, if using. Fry until the oil rises to the surface.
Stir in the rice to coat every grain. Add stock to just cover the rice and season with salt — it should taste slightly over-salted.
Cover the pot tightly with foil, then the lid. Cook on the lowest heat without stirring.

Check the rice. If it is still hard, sprinkle over a little water, re-cover and cook 5–10 minutes more. A thin, lightly scorched layer at the bottom gives the prized smoky "party" flavour — don't stir it in until the end.
Fluff with a fork, stir in the butter if using, and rest covered for 5 minutes before serving.

tips: Parboiled long-grain rice keeps its shape best; basmati works but needs less liquid.
Too little liquid is easier to fix than too much — add water in small splashes.
recipes.serving: With fried plantain, coleslaw, fried or grilled chicken, or moin moin.
recipes.culture: Nigeria, Ghana and Senegal all claim the best jollof, and the friendly rivalry is a running joke across West Africa. The dish is generally traced to the Wolof people of the Senegambia region.

changes: use vegetable stock instead of chicken stock
use vegetable stock instead of chicken stock
use vegetable stock instead of chicken stock

recipes.title: Boerenkool Stamppot
recipes.summary: Buttery mashed potatoes with finely chopped kale, served with a smoked sausage — Dutch winter comfort food.

items.prep: stems removed and very finely chopped
items.name: kale

steps.text: Put the potatoes in a pot with salted water to just cover, and lay the kale on top. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer until the potatoes are soft. Heat the sausage in a pan of hot (not boiling) water at the same time.
Drain the potatoes and kale well, then mash them together with the butter and enough warm milk to make a coarse, fluffy mash.
Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper. Serve with the sliced sausage.

tips: Make a hollow in each portion for a pool of gravy (a "kuiltje jus").
recipes.serving: With mustard and gravy.

recipes.title: Fårikål
recipes.summary: Norway's national dish — mutton and cabbage layered with whole black peppercorns and simmered slowly until meltingly tender.

items.prep: on the bone, cut into pieces
items.name: lamb shoulder

items.prep: cut into wedges with the core
items.name: white cabbage

steps.text: Layer the meat (fatty side down first) and cabbage in a heavy pot, sprinkling each layer with salt, peppercorns and a little flour.
Pour in the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer very gently until the meat falls off the bone.

recipes.serving: With boiled potatoes and lingonberry jam.

recipes.title: Momo
recipes.summary: Juicy steamed dumplings filled with spiced minced chicken, served with a fiery roasted tomato and sesame achar.

steps.text: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the filling ingredients well with your hand until sticky.
For the achar, char the tomatoes and chilies in a dry pan or over a flame, then blend with the rest of the achar ingredients.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 30 pieces and roll each into a thin 8 cm circle, thinner at the edges.
Put a spoonful of filling in the centre and pleat the edges together, twisting to seal at the top.
Steam on an oiled steamer tray, not touching, until the wrappers are translucent and the filling is cooked.

recipes.serving: Hot, with the achar for dipping.
recipes.culture: Brought to Nepal by Newar traders from Tibet, momo is now Nepal's most popular snack, sold everywhere from street stalls to restaurants.

changes: use vegetable oil instead of butter

recipes.title: Pavlova
recipes.summary: A meringue with a crisp shell and soft marshmallow centre, piled with whipped cream and fresh fruit.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 120 °C. Draw a 20 cm circle on baking paper and flip it over on a tray.

Whisk the egg whites in a very clean bowl to soft peaks. Add the sugar a spoonful at a time, whisking until the meringue is thick, glossy and the sugar has dissolved (rub a little between your fingers — it shouldn't feel gritty).
Fold in the cornstarch, vinegar and vanilla.
Spread the meringue within the circle, building up the sides slightly.
Bake until the outside is crisp and dry.
Turn off the oven, prop the door ajar and let the pavlova cool completely inside. This stops it cracking too much.
Just before serving, whip the cream to soft peaks, spread it over the top and pile on the fruit.

recipes.culture: Named after the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova, who toured both countries in the 1920s. Australia and New Zealand have argued over who invented it ever since.

changes: use vanilla bean instead of vanilla extract

recipes.title: Sancocho de Gallina
recipes.summary: Panama's national dish — a clear, restorative chicken soup with yam, culantro and oregano.

steps.text: Simmer the chicken with the onion, garlic, half the cilantro, oregano and salt, skimming, until tender.
Add the yam (and corn) and simmer until the yam is soft and some has dissolved to thicken the broth.
Chop the remaining cilantro, stir it in, and season.

recipes.serving: With white rice on the side, added to the bowl as you eat.
recipes.culture: Known as "levanta muertos" (raise the dead) — the cure for a hangover or a cold.

recipes.title: Ceviche
recipes.summary: Very fresh white fish cured for minutes in lime juice with chili, red onion and cilantro, served with sweet potato and corn.

items.note: sushi-grade sea bass, sole or corvina
items.name: firm white fish

items.note: freshly squeezed from about 12 small limes — don't squeeze too hard or it turns bitter
items.name: lime juice

items.prep: very thinly sliced, rinsed in cold water
items.name: red onion

steps.text: Boil the sweet potato and corn until tender; let them cool.
Keep everything cold. Put the fish in a chilled bowl, season with salt and toss.
Add the garlic and chili, then pour over the lime juice and toss.
Leave just until the outside of the fish turns opaque while the centre stays translucent.
Fold in the onion and cilantro. Serve immediately on lettuce with sweet potato and corn.

tips: Peruvian ceviche is cured briefly — a few minutes, not hours.
Use fish labelled for raw consumption or previously frozen fish to reduce the risk of parasites.
recipes.serving: The leftover juice, leche de tigre, is drunk from a small glass.
recipes.culture: Ceviche's preparation and consumption were inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list as an expression of Peruvian traditional cuisine in 2023.

recipes.title: Chicken Adobo
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves and black pepper until tender and glazed.

steps.text: Combine the chicken with the soy sauce and garlic and leave to marinate.
Put the chicken and marinade in a pot with the vinegar, bay leaves, peppercorns and water. Bring to a boil and let it bubble for 2 minutes without stirring — this mellows the vinegar.
Cover and simmer gently until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken. Brown it skin-side down in the oil in a frying pan.
Meanwhile, reduce the sauce until syrupy. Add the sugar if you like it rounder, then return the chicken and turn to coat.

recipes.serving: With steamed rice to soak up the sauce.
recipes.culture: There are as many adobos as Filipino households — with pork, coconut milk, extra vinegar, or no soy sauce at all (adobong puti).

recipes.title: Chicken Karahi
recipes.summary: Chicken cooked fast and hot in a wok-like karahi with fresh tomatoes, ginger, garlic and green chilies until the sauce clings.

items.note: half grated, half cut into thin matchsticks
items.name: fresh ginger

steps.text: Heat the oil in the karahi over high heat. Add the chicken and fry, turning, until it loses its raw colour (5 minutes).
Add the grated ginger, garlic and salt and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, cover, and cook over medium-high heat until they have completely broken down. Remove any loose tomato skins.
Uncover, add the chili powder, chili flakes, coriander, cumin and pepper, and stir-fry over high heat — pressing and turning — until the oil separates from a thick masala that coats the chicken.
Stir in the yogurt if using and cook 2 minutes. Add the green chilies, ginger matchsticks and garam masala and toss for 1 minute.
Finish with cilantro and serve from the karahi.

recipes.serving: With naan or roti, sliced onion and lemon.
recipes.culture: Named after the cast-iron pan it's cooked and served in; roadside karahi restaurants on the Grand Trunk Road are famous for it.

recipes.title: Pierogi Ruskie
recipes.summary: Half-moon dumplings filled with potato, tangy farmer's cheese and fried onion, boiled and topped with more onions in butter.

steps.text: Mix the dough ingredients and knead for 5–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until soft, drain and mash. Fry the onion in butter until golden. Mix the potato, cheese, onion, salt and pepper and let it cool.
Roll the dough thinly (about 2 mm) and cut out rounds. Place a teaspoon of filling in the middle, fold over and pinch the edges tightly to seal, crimping if you like.
Cook the pierogi in batches in a large pot of salted, gently boiling water. When they float, cook 2 minutes more and lift out.
Fry the chopped onion in butter until golden and pour over the pierogi. Serve with sour cream.

tips: Leftover boiled pierogi are excellent pan-fried in butter the next day.
Freeze uncooked pierogi on a tray, then bag them; cook from frozen.
recipes.culture: "Ruskie" refers to Red Ruthenia, the historical region around Lviv, not to Russia.

recipes.title: Musakhan
recipes.summary: Roast chicken on flatbread soaked with olive oil, piled with slow-cooked onions and lots of tangy sumac.

items.note: large taboon or markook bread is traditional
items.name: pita bread

steps.text: Rub the chicken with the spices, salt and oil and marinate.
Roast at 200 °C until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile cook the onions slowly in the olive oil with a pinch of salt until very soft and sweet but not browned (about 30 minutes). Stir in the sumac.
Lay the breads on a tray, brush with oil from the onions, spread with the onions, and top with the chicken.
Bake until the bread edges crisp.
Scatter with pine nuts and more sumac.

recipes.serving: Eaten by hand, tearing the soaked bread, with yogurt and salad.
recipes.culture: Traditionally made after the olive harvest to celebrate the fresh new oil.

recipes.title: Caldo Verde
recipes.summary: A silky potato and onion soup with ribbons of finely shredded kale, served with a slice of smoky chouriço.

items.prep: stems removed, rolled and cut into very fine ribbons
items.name: kale

steps.text: Warm 2 tablespoons oil and soften the onion and garlic. Add potatoes, water and salt.
Simmer until the potatoes are very soft.
Blend until completely smooth.
Bring back to a boil, add the kale and cook uncovered until tender but still bright green.
Meanwhile, fry the chouriço slices briefly. Serve each bowl with a slice or two of chouriço and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.serving: With broa (Portuguese corn bread).

recipes.title: Sopa Paraguaya
recipes.summary: A rich, savoury cornbread made with cheese, onions and milk — despite its name, a "soup" you cut into squares.

items.note: Paraguayan queso Paraguay or another fresh melting cheese
items.name: queso fresco

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C and grease the dish.
Cook the onions slowly in the butter with the salt until very soft but not browned. Cool slightly.
Beat the eggs, then mix in the milk, cheese, onions with their butter, and finally the cornmeal. The batter should be thick but pourable; rest 5 minutes.
Pour into the dish and bake until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes before cutting into squares.

recipes.serving: Alongside asado (grilled meat) and chipa guasu.
recipes.culture: One popular story says a cook to the 19th-century president Carlos Antonio López added too much corn flour to his soup — and the "solid soup" was a hit.

recipes.title: Mămăligă with Cheese and Sour Cream
recipes.summary: Soft, golden cornmeal porridge topped with salty crumbled sheep's cheese and cool sour cream.

items.note: Romanian telemea or brânză de burduf
items.name: feta

steps.text: Bring the salted water to a boil. Pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Switch to a wooden spoon and cook over low heat, stirring often, until thick and it pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the butter.
Spoon onto plates and top with the cheese, sour cream and a fried egg if you like.

tips: For a firm mămăligă that can be sliced (traditionally with a thread), cook it longer and turn it out onto a board.
recipes.serving: Also as a side for sarmale (cabbage rolls) or tochitură (pork stew).

recipes.title: Gibanica
recipes.summary: A golden, layered pie of crumpled phyllo baked with eggs and soft white cheese — a fixture of Serbian holidays and breakfasts.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C and oil the dish.
Whisk the eggs, cheeses, milk, half the oil, baking powder and salt.
Lay 2 sheets of phyllo in the dish and brush with oil. Dip the remaining sheets one by one in the egg mixture, crumple loosely and pack them in the dish. Top with 2 flat sheets brushed with oil.
Pour over any remaining egg mixture.
Bake until puffed and deep golden.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

recipes.serving: Warm, with plain yogurt.

recipes.title: Blini
recipes.summary: Thin, lacy pancakes brushed with butter and stacked high, served with sour cream, jam or caviar.
equipment: 24 cm frying pan or crêpe pan

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, sugar and salt, then whisk in half the milk.
Add the flour and whisk to a thick, smooth batter, then whisk in the remaining milk and the oil.
Rest the batter.
Heat the lightly greased pan over medium-high heat. Pour in a small ladle of batter and swirl to coat the pan thinly.
Cook until the edges are lacy and golden underneath (about 1 minute), flip and cook 30 seconds more.
Stack the blini, brushing each with melted butter.

recipes.serving: Folded into quarters, with smetana (sour cream), jam, honey, or salmon roe.
recipes.culture: Round, golden blini symbolise the sun at Maslenitsa, the week-long festival that ends winter before Orthodox Lent.

recipes.title: Agatogo
recipes.summary: Green cooking bananas stewed with beef, tomato, palm oil and greens — a hearty Rwandan one-pot meal.

steps.text: Brown the beef in the oil, then add the onion and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes, pepper, carrots, water and salt and simmer, covered, until the beef is nearly tender.
Add the bananas and simmer until soft and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the spinach for the last 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Chicken Kabsa
recipes.summary: Chicken and basmati rice cooked together with tomato, dried lime and warm spices, topped with toasted almonds and raisins.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and soak it in cold water.
Fry the onions in the oil until golden, then add garlic and the chicken and brown the chicken on all sides.
Add the tomato, tomato paste, carrot, dried lime and all the spices and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the water and salt, cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked.
Lift out the chicken and keep warm (traditionally it is browned under the grill). Measure about 750 ml of broth back into the pot.
Add the drained rice, bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat until tender.
Spread the rice on a platter, top with the chicken, almonds and raisins.

recipes.serving: On a large shared platter, with daqqus (spiced tomato sauce) and salad.

recipes.title: Ful Medames
recipes.summary: Mashed fava beans dressed Sudanese-style with sesame oil, cumin and lime, topped with white cheese, tomato and onion.

steps.text: Simmer the beans with their liquid until hot and soft.
Mash roughly with the cumin, garlic and salt.
Spoon into a bowl, pour over the sesame oil and lime, and top with tomato, onion, chili and cheese.

recipes.serving: Shared from one bowl with bread, often with ta'amiya (falafel) on top.

recipes.title: Swedish Meatballs
recipes.summary: Small, tender beef-and-pork meatballs with a creamy brown gravy, lingonberry jam and potatoes.

items.prep: finely chopped and softened in butter
items.name: onion

steps.text: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Mix in the onion, meat, egg, allspice, salt and pepper until evenly combined. Roll into balls about 3 cm across with wet hands.
Fry the meatballs in butter in batches over medium heat, shaking the pan so they stay round, until browned and cooked through.
For the gravy, stir the flour into the fat left in the pan and cook 1 minute. Whisk in the stock, then the cream and soy sauce, and simmer until thickened.
Serve meatballs and gravy with potatoes and lingonberry jam.

recipes.serving: Traditionally with pressgurka (quick-pickled cucumber) too.

changes: use minced beef instead of minced pork

recipes.title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
recipes.summary: Silky poached chicken with rice cooked in its fragrant broth, served with chili-ginger sauce, dark soy and cucumber.

steps.text: Rub the chicken all over with salt, rinse, and stuff the cavity with ginger and scallions.
Bring the water to a boil, lower in the chicken breast-side down, return to a bare simmer and cook gently.
Turn off the heat, cover and leave the chicken in the hot water until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 74 °C.
Plunge the chicken into iced water for 10 minutes to firm the skin, then rub with sesame oil. Keep the broth.

Fry the garlic and shallot in the oil until fragrant, add the rice and stir to coat. Add 550 ml of the chicken broth, the pandan and a pinch of salt, and cook as for plain rice (covered, low heat, 15 minutes, then rest 10).
Blend the chili sauce ingredients with 3 tablespoons of broth.
Carve the chicken and serve with the rice, chili sauce, dark soy, cucumber, cilantro and a bowl of broth.

recipes.culture: Brought by migrants from Hainan island in southern China and reinvented in Singapore, where it is often called the national dish.

recipes.title: Jota
recipes.summary: A thick, smoky soup of beans, potatoes and sauerkraut thickened with a paprika roux — from the Slovenian Karst and Trieste.

steps.text: Simmer the drained beans in the water with the bay leaves (and the smoked meat, if using) until the beans are tender.
Add the potatoes and sauerkraut and simmer until the potatoes are soft.
Mash some of the potatoes and beans against the side of the pot to thicken.
Make a roux (prežganje) by frying the flour in the oil until golden; off the heat stir in the garlic and paprika, then stir it into the soup and simmer 5 minutes. Season.

recipes.title: Bryndzové Halušky
recipes.summary: Slovakia's national dish — little potato dumplings tossed with tangy sheep's-cheese bryndza and topped with crispy bacon.

items.note: approximately — enough for a thick, sticky dough
items.name: all-purpose flour

steps.text: Mix the grated potato, egg, salt and enough flour to make a soft, sticky dough that holds on a spoon.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the dough through the halušky board (or scrape small pieces off a board with a knife) into the water.
When the dumplings rise, boil 1 minute more, lift out and drain.
Fry the bacon until crisp.
Toss the hot halušky with the bryndza (and a spoonful of bacon fat) until creamy. Serve topped with bacon and chives.

recipes.serving: With a glass of žinčica (sheep's whey) or buttermilk.

recipes.title: Chicken Yassa
recipes.summary: Chicken marinated in lemon, mustard and chili, then simmered in a mountain of slow-caramelised onions.

steps.text: Mix the chicken, onions, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, chili, half the oil, salt and pepper. Marinate in the fridge.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade and grill or pan-fry until browned on both sides (it needn't be cooked through).
Heat the rest of the oil in a large pot. Lift the onions out of the marinade and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add the remaining marinade, the bouillon cube if using, bay leaves and 150 ml water. Return the chicken to the pot.
Cover and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce is jammy. Add the olives for the last 5 minutes.
Taste for salt and sharpness — it should be tangy.

recipes.serving: Over plain white rice.

recipes.title: Bariis Iskukaris
recipes.summary: Basmati rice cooked with tender lamb, tomato and xawaash — Somalia's warm, cardamom-and-cinnamon spice blend.

items.note: for the meat, then the rice
items.name: water

items.note: blended with lime and cilantro as basbaas
items.name: fresh green chili

steps.text: Rinse the rice and soak it in cold water.
Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy pot. Add the onion and cook until golden, then the garlic, tomato, paste, xawaash, cinnamon and cloves. Fry for 2 minutes.
Add 500 ml water and 1 teaspoon salt, cover and simmer until the lamb is tender.
Drain the rice and add it with the raisins, 700 ml water and the rest of the salt. The liquid should sit about 1 cm above the rice.
Bring to a boil, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat until the rice is tender.
Rest 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

recipes.serving: Traditionally eaten with a banana on the side and a spicy green chili sauce (basbaas).
recipes.culture: Bananas with rice are a legacy of Somalia's agricultural south; the spice trade along the Somali coast shaped xawaash.

recipes.title: Pupusas
recipes.summary: Thick corn tortillas stuffed with refried beans and melting cheese, griddled and eaten with tangy cabbage curtido and tomato salsa.
occasions: National Pupusa Day (second Sunday of November)

items.note: for your hands and the griddle
items.name: vegetable oil

steps.text: Mix the curtido ingredients, pour over boiling water to cover for 1 minute, drain, then add the vinegar, water, oregano, salt and chili. Leave to pickle.
Mix the masa harina, salt and warm water into a soft dough that doesn't crack when pressed — like play dough. Divide into 8 balls.
With oiled hands, flatten a ball into a cup in your palm, add a spoonful each of beans and cheese, close the dough around it and pat gently into a 1 cm thick disc.
Cook on a medium-hot griddle until browned in spots on both sides and the cheese is melting.
Serve hot with curtido and tomato salsa.

recipes.serving: Eaten by hand, torn and topped with curtido.

recipes.title: Muhammara
recipes.summary: A rich, sweet-smoky dip of roasted red peppers, toasted walnuts and pomegranate molasses from Aleppo.

items.note: or 1 tbsp Turkish red pepper paste
items.name: Aleppo pepper

steps.text: Roast the peppers under a hot grill or over a flame, turning, until blackened all over.
Steam them in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and deseed.
Pulse the walnuts in the processor until coarsely ground. Add everything else and pulse to a textured paste — not completely smooth.
Taste and balance the sweet, sour and heat. Serve drizzled with olive oil and a few walnuts.

recipes.serving: With warm flatbread, as part of a mezze spread or with grilled meats.

recipes.title: Pad Kra Pao
recipes.summary: Minced chicken flash-fried with garlic, chilies and peppery holy basil, served over rice with a crisp-edged fried egg.

steps.text: Pound the garlic and chilies to a coarse paste in a mortar (or chop finely).
If making fried eggs, fry them first in the hot oil until the whites are puffed and crisp at the edges. Set aside.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the garlic-chili paste for a few seconds, then add the chicken, breaking it up.
Add the sauces, sugar and water and stir-fry until the chicken is cooked and glossy (about 3 minutes).
Turn off the heat and toss in the basil until just wilted.
Serve over rice, topped with the fried egg.

tips: Holy basil (kra pao) is peppery and clove-like; Thai sweet basil is a different but tasty substitute.
recipes.serving: With a little dish of prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies).

recipes.title: Qurutob
recipes.summary: Tajikistan's national dish — torn flaky flatbread soaked in a salty yogurt sauce, topped with onions fried in oil, tomatoes and herbs.

items.note: Tajik fatir or another flaky flatbread, torn into pieces
items.name: pita bread

steps.text: Blend the yogurt, feta and water into a thin, salty, sour sauce. (Traditionally this is made by dissolving qurut — dried salted yogurt balls — in warm water.)
Fry the onions in the oil until golden.
Spread the bread pieces on a large platter and pour over the sauce. Let it soak in for a few minutes.
Top with the onions and their hot oil, then the tomatoes, cucumber, herbs and chili.

recipes.serving: Eaten by hand from a shared wooden platter (tabaq).

recipes.title: Shakshuka
recipes.summary: Eggs gently poached in a spiced pepper and tomato sauce with harissa and caraway.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and pepper over medium heat until soft (about 8 minutes).
Add garlic, harissa and spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and salt and simmer, crushing the tomatoes, until thick.
Make hollows in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook over low heat until the whites are set but the yolks still runny (5–8 minutes).
Scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan.

recipes.serving: With crusty bread for dipping.
recipes.culture: A North African dish, carried to Israel by Tunisian and Libyan Jewish immigrants, where it became a breakfast staple.

recipes.title: ʻOta ʻIka
recipes.summary: Raw fish cured in lime and bathed in plenty of coconut cream with crunchy vegetables and chili.

steps.text: Toss the fish with the lime juice and salt, cover and chill until opaque around the edges.
Drain off most of the juice and mix in the coconut cream and vegetables. Serve cold.

tips: Use fish labelled for raw consumption or previously frozen fish.
recipes.serving: With boiled taro, cassava or sweet potato.

recipes.title: Red Lentil Soup
recipes.summary: A velvety soup of red lentils, onion and carrot, finished with a drizzle of butter and Aleppo pepper and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Heat the oil and soften the onion, carrot and potato for 5 minutes. Stir in the paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the lentils, cumin and water. Simmer until the lentils and vegetables are completely soft.
Blend until smooth. Season and add water if it is too thick.
Melt the butter until it foams, take it off the heat and stir in the Aleppo pepper and mint.
Ladle the soup into bowls, drizzle with the red butter and serve with lemon.

recipes.serving: With bread and lemon — a classic start to a meal, and a lokanta (canteen) staple.

changes: use olive oil instead of butter
use olive oil instead of butter

recipes.title: Pelau
recipes.summary: Chicken browned in caramelised sugar, then cooked with rice, pigeon peas and coconut milk in one pot — a Trinidad and Tobago favourite.

steps.text: Blend the cilantro, scallions, garlic and thyme with a splash of water. Rub it and the salt into the chicken.
Marinate the chicken.
Heat the oil and sugar in a heavy pot over medium heat until the sugar melts, froths and turns dark amber (watch closely — seconds separate dark from burnt).
Immediately add the chicken, stirring to coat it in the caramel. Cook, covered, for 10 minutes until well coloured.
Add the onion, carrot and rice and stir for 2 minutes. Add the peas, coconut milk, water and the whole pepper and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed. Remove the pepper.

recipes.serving: With coleslaw, sliced cucumber and pepper sauce.

recipes.title: Chipsi Mayai
recipes.summary: Freshly fried chips set into an omelette — Tanzania's beloved street food, served with kachumbari salad.

steps.text: Mix the kachumbari ingredients with a pinch of salt.
Fry the chips until golden and cooked through. Drain and salt.
Put half the chips in a small, lightly oiled non-stick pan over medium heat. Beat 2 eggs with a pinch of salt and pour over the chips.
Cook until the base is set, then flip (using a plate) and cook 1–2 minutes more. Repeat.

recipes.serving: With kachumbari, ketchup and chili sauce.

recipes.title: Borshch
recipes.summary: A deep-red soup of beetroot, cabbage, potato and beef broth, sharpened with a little acid and served with sour cream and dill.

steps.text: Simmer the beef in the water with the bay leaves, skimming off foam, until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, cut it into pieces and return it to the broth. (For a meatless borshch, simply start with water or vegetable stock and add the beans with the cabbage.)

Meanwhile, fry the onion and carrot in the oil until soft. Add the beetroot, tomato paste, vinegar and sugar with a splash of broth, and braise until tender (15 minutes). The acid keeps the beetroot red.
Add the potatoes to the simmering broth and cook for 10 minutes, then add the cabbage and cook 5 minutes more.
Stir in the beetroot mixture and garlic, season, and bring just to a simmer. Turn off the heat and let it stand covered for 15 minutes.

recipes.serving: With a spoonful of sour cream, dill, and pampushky (garlic bread rolls) or rye bread.
recipes.culture: The culture of Ukrainian borshch cooking was inscribed on UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding in 2022.

changes: use canned red kidney beans instead of beef shank
