recipes.title: Rolex
recipes.summary: Uganda's favourite street snack — a vegetable omelette rolled up in a soft, flaky chapati.

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt, water and 1 tablespoon oil into a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide in two. Roll each thin, brush with oil, roll up into a rope, coil it and roll out again into a 22 cm round — this makes flaky layers.
Cook the chapatis on a hot dry pan, brushing with oil, until golden-spotted on both sides. Keep warm.
Beat 2 eggs with half the vegetables and salt. Pour into the oiled pan and cook until almost set.
Lay a chapati on top of the omelette, press, then flip together so the chapati warms. Roll up tightly. Repeat.

recipes.serving: Wrapped in paper and eaten hot from street stalls, especially around Kampala.
recipes.culture: The name is a play on "rolled eggs"; Uganda celebrates the snack with an annual Rolex Festival.

recipes.title: Red Beans and Rice
recipes.summary: Red kidney beans simmered for hours with smoked sausage and the Creole "holy trinity" until creamy, served over white rice.

steps.text: Brown the sausage in the oil in a heavy pot. Remove with a slotted spoon.
Cook the onion, pepper and celery in the fat until soft (8 minutes). Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the drained beans, sausage, bay, thyme, cayenne, black pepper and water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer, partly covered, stirring occasionally, until the beans are very soft.
Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot and simmer uncovered until creamy. Season with salt.
Serve over rice with scallions and hot sauce.

recipes.culture: Traditionally cooked on Mondays — washday in New Orleans — when the pot could simmer unattended using the bone left over from Sunday's ham.

recipes.title: Chivito
recipes.summary: Uruguay's towering steak sandwich — thin beef, ham, bacon, melted mozzarella and a fried egg, with lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise.

items.note: thin slices of tenderloin, about 120 g each
items.name: beef steak

steps.text: Fry the bacon until crisp. Fry the eggs.
Season the steaks and sear them on a very hot griddle for 1 minute per side. Top each with ham and mozzarella and cover briefly so the cheese melts.
Spread the rolls with mayonnaise and layer lettuce, tomato, the steak stack, bacon and egg. Add olives if you like.

recipes.serving: With fries or Russian salad (ensalada rusa).

recipes.title: Plov
recipes.summary: Lamb, sweet yellow carrots and rice slowly cooked together in a cast-iron kazan with whole heads of garlic and cumin.
equipment: Cast-iron kazan or heavy Dutch oven

items.note: yellow carrots if you can find them
items.name: carrot

items.note: whole heads, outer papery skin removed
items.name: garlic

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water is clear, then soak it in warm salted water.
Heat the oil in the kazan until very hot. Brown the lamb in batches until well seared.
Add the onions and fry until golden. Spread the carrots over the top without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and fry until they soften (about 10 minutes).
Add cumin, coriander, barberries, half the salt and enough boiling water to just cover. Simmer — this broth, the zirvak, is the soul of plov.
Drain the rice and spread it in an even layer over the zirvak — do not stir. Add boiling water to cover the rice by 1.5 cm and the rest of the salt. Push the garlic heads into the rice.

Boil on high until the water disappears below the surface of the rice. Gather the rice into a dome, poke a few holes to the bottom with a spoon handle, cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Mix gently, or serve layered — rice on a big platter topped with carrots, meat and garlic.

recipes.serving: On a shared platter with achichuk (tomato and onion salad) and green tea.
recipes.culture: Uzbekistan's palov culture was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2016. Making plov for a crowd is traditionally a man's job, and it is the centrepiece of weddings and celebrations.

recipes.title: Arepas
recipes.summary: Crisp-crusted, soft-centred corn cakes made from precooked maize flour, split and stuffed with cheese, beans or anything at all.

items.note: precooked white maize flour, such as Harina P.A.N.
items.name: masarepa

items.note: queso blanco or queso de mano
items.name: queso fresco

steps.text: Mix the water and salt, then gradually add the masarepa, working it with your hand until there are no lumps.
Rest the dough so it hydrates. It should be soft and not crack at the edges when pressed; add water if it does.
Divide into 6 balls and flatten into discs about 1.5 cm thick.

Heat the lightly oiled pan over medium heat and cook the arepas for 5–6 minutes per side until a crust forms. Finish in a 180 °C oven for 10 minutes, or keep cooking on the pan until they sound hollow when tapped.
Split open with a knife, spread with butter and stuff with cheese and beans.

recipes.serving: For breakfast with coffee. Famous fillings include reina pepiada (chicken-avocado salad) and pabellón (shredded beef, black beans and plantain).

recipes.title: Fresh Spring Rolls
recipes.summary: Rice paper rolled around shrimp, pork, rice noodles and fresh herbs, dipped in a peanut-hoisin sauce.

steps.text: If using pork, simmer it in salted water until cooked through (about 25 minutes). Cool and slice thinly.
Poach the shrimp in boiling water for 2 minutes, cool, peel and halve lengthwise.
Cook the vermicelli according to the packet, rinse in cold water and drain well.
Dip a rice paper in warm water for 2–3 seconds and lay it on a damp board. It will soften as you work.

Lay lettuce, a little noodles and herbs on the lower third. Fold the bottom over, roll once, place three shrimp halves (cut side up) and pork above, fold in the sides and roll tightly, tucking a chive in so it sticks out.
Simmer the hoisin, peanut butter and water for 1 minute, stirring until smooth. Top with peanuts and chili.

tips: Rolls are best within a couple of hours; cover with a damp cloth so they don't dry out.

recipes.title: Sapasui
recipes.summary: Glass noodles soaked up in a garlicky soy and ginger braise with beef — a Samoan party staple.

steps.text: Soak the noodles in warm water until soft, then drain and cut into shorter lengths with scissors.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil until fragrant. Add the beef and stir-fry until browned.
Add the soy sauce, sugar and water and simmer until the beef is tender.
Add the noodles and cabbage and toss over the heat until the noodles have absorbed most of the liquid.

recipes.culture: Introduced by Chinese labourers who came to Samoa in the early 1900s and since adopted as a fixture of every Samoan feast.

recipes.title: Saltah
recipes.summary: Yemen's national dish — a bubbling lamb broth stew with vegetables, crowned with a frothy, bitter-green fenugreek topping (hulba).

steps.text: Soak the ground fenugreek in the water until it forms a gel. Pour off the water.
Simmer the lamb in the water until tender, then shred the meat and keep the broth (maraq).
Blend the soaked fenugreek with the cilantro, chili, garlic, lemon and salt, then whisk vigorously with a few spoonfuls of cold water until pale and frothy, like whipped egg white.
In the stone pot, fry the onion, garlic, tomato, chili, potato and spices in the oil until soft. Add 500 ml of broth and the shredded meat and boil hard until thick.
Crack in the eggs if using and stir. Spoon the hulba over the top and bring to the table still bubbling.

recipes.serving: Scooped up with flatbread (malawah or khubz), with the remaining broth drunk alongside.

recipes.title: Bobotie
recipes.summary: Gently curried minced beef with fruit and almonds, baked under a savoury egg custard — a Cape Malay classic.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Soak the bread in the milk.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the onions until soft. Add the garlic, curry powder and turmeric and fry for 1 minute.
Add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until it loses its pink colour.

Squeeze the milk out of the bread (keep the milk) and mash the bread into the mince with the chutney, raisins, lemon juice, almonds, salt and pepper. Taste — it should be gently sweet, sour and spiced.
Press the mixture into the dish.
Whisk the eggs into the reserved milk with a pinch of salt and pour it over the meat. Tuck the bay leaves into the top.
Bake until the custard is set and golden.

recipes.serving: With geelrys (yellow rice with raisins), sliced banana, and blatjang (fruit chutney).
recipes.culture: Bobotie reflects the Cape's history — Southeast Asian spice traditions brought by enslaved and exiled people from the Dutch East Indies, combined with Dutch baking.

recipes.title: Ifisashi
recipes.summary: Leafy greens and tomato simmered in a creamy sauce of ground peanuts, eaten with nshima.

items.note: or pumpkin leaves or rape greens
items.name: kale

items.note: cooked as for ugali (see the Kenyan recipe)
items.name: white maize flour

steps.text: Simmer the ground peanuts in the water with the onion and tomato, stirring, until creamy (about 10 minutes).
Add the greens and salt and simmer gently, stirring now and then, until tender and the sauce coats the leaves.
Serve with nshima.

recipes.title: Dovi
recipes.summary: Chicken simmered with tomato, onion and peppers in a rich peanut butter sauce, served with sadza.

items.note: cooked as for ugali (see the Kenyan recipe)
items.name: white maize flour

steps.text: Brown the chicken in the oil. Add the onion, garlic and pepper and cook until soft.
Add the tomatoes, water and salt, cover and simmer until the chicken is nearly cooked.
Mix the peanut butter with a ladle of hot liquid until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Simmer gently, stirring often so it doesn't catch, until the sauce is thick. Add the greens for the last 5 minutes.
Serve with sadza.
